balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Serko Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Serko Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Serko Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Serko Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Serko Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Serko Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Serko Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Serko Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Serko Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Serko Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

subscription.title: Subscription mix
subscription.content:
Subscription revenue is recurring; services revenue (implementation, training) is lower-margin and lumpy.

For Serko Limited: a rising subscription share improves gross margin and predictability.

What to watch:

  • Subscription as a share of total revenue

revenueMix.title: Revenue by stream
revenueMix.content:
Serko does not sell software subscriptions. It earns travel platform booking revenue (its share of hotel supplier commissions on Booking.com for Business, recognised on completed stays), supplier commissions revenue earned directly from suppliers, services revenue (implementation, support), and other revenue.

For Serko Limited: the Booking.com for Business platform revenue is the single largest stream and is contractually tiered -- the take-rate steps down as Completed Room Nights (CRN) rise (roughly 50% below 4.3m CRN, ~40% blended at 6m, ~32% at 8.6m). Serko hit 4.3m CRN in FY2026, so this stream can keep growing in dollars while its margin quality falls. That tension is the central risk in the DCF.

What to watch:

  • Travel platform booking revenue growing slower than CRN growth (the tier stepping down)
  • Supplier commissions and services diversifying away from the single Booking.com relationship
  • Contract renewal terms at the 31-Mar-2029 expiry

totalIncome.title: Revenue vs total income
totalIncome.content:
Revenue is operating revenue from customers and platform partners. Total income adds interest income earned on Serko's cash and deposit balances and any other non-operating income.

For Serko Limited: with no debt and a sizeable cash/deposit balance, interest income is a real but non-operating contributor -- EBITDAFI (below) is management's own metric for folding it in.

What to watch:

  • The gap between the two lines widening as interest rates or cash balances change, not as the underlying business improves

platformExpense.title: Platform revenue vs platform expense
platformExpense.content:
Platform expense is the direct cost of servicing Booking.com for Business volume (data, processing, supplier-facing costs), set against the travel platform booking revenue it generates.

For Serko Limited: because the Booking.com commission tier steps down with volume, watch whether platform expense grows in line with CRN (volume-linked, healthy) or faster than platform revenue (margin compression on top of the tier step-down).

What to watch:

  • Platform expense as a share of platform revenue trending up
  • Whether cost scales with CRN or with revenue dollars

capDev.title: Capitalised development costs
capDev.content:
Software development spend that meets the accounting criteria to be capitalised as an intangible asset rather than expensed immediately, then amortised over its useful life.

For Serko Limited: capitalised development understates near-term opex and overstates near-term profit versus a company that expenses all R&D; the DCF's owner-FCF treats this spend as a cash cost regardless of its accounting treatment.

What to watch:

  • Capitalised development rising as a share of total R&D spend (a red flag for earnings quality)
  • Amortisation of prior capitalised costs flowing back through the income statement

ebitdaFi.title: EBITDAFI
ebitdaFi.content:
EBITDAFI (EBITDA + interest income, sometimes stated as EBITDA before finance income) is Serko's own headline profitability metric, folding in interest earned on its cash and deposits.

For Serko Limited: management guides the market to EBITDAFI, not statutory EBITDA -- the gap between the two lines is entirely the interest income the company earns on a debt-free balance sheet with a large cash/deposit pile.

What to watch:

  • EBITDAFI turning positive (management's stated inflection target) versus EBITDA remaining negative
  • How much of any EBITDAFI improvement is operating leverage versus rising interest income

cashDeposits.title: Cash, short-term deposits and total cash & deposits
cashDeposits.content:
Cash & equivalents plus short-term deposits (term deposits not classified as cash) sum to total cash & deposits, Serko's full liquid balance-sheet buffer.

For Serko Limited: with zero interest-bearing debt, this combined balance is the funding runway for the path to EBITDAFI breakeven and the source of the interest income in EBITDAFI and total income above.

What to watch:

  • Total cash & deposits trend versus the cash burn implied by owner FCF
  • Shift between cash and term deposits (a treasury choice, not a funding change)

nta.title: Net tangible assets per share
nta.content:
NTA per share is (total assets less intangible assets less total liabilities) divided by shares outstanding, in cents -- a hard-asset floor that excludes capitalised development costs and goodwill.

For Serko Limited: because a large share of the balance sheet is capitalised development costs (an intangible), NTA per share sits well below reported book value per share and is a more conservative reference point for a loss-making company with no proven path to profit.

What to watch:

  • NTA per share trend versus the cash burn (owner FCF) funding the losses
  • How much of book equity is intangible (capitalised development) versus tangible
